findings.detail: The shipped gloss takes kaikki's first sense, the literal 'run a household', which is the dated reading; modern usage is overwhelmingly 'mit etwas haushalten' — to use a resource sparingly (mit den Kräften/Ressourcen/dem Geld haushalten). DWDS and Duden both give the economizing sense as the live one, and it is candidate_glosses index 1. A learner meeting haushalten in text will almost always meet it with 'mit' plus a resource, not as a synonym for einen Haushalt führen.

The shipped gloss takes kaikki's first sense, the narrow figurative one that only works in the frame 'es brach aus ihm heraus' (words bursting out of someone). The sense a learner meets is the literal one at candidate_glosses index 1: forcibly breaking a piece out of something, or a piece breaking off (einen Zahn herausbrechen, ein Stück aus der Mauer herausbrechen). Standing alone as English, 'burst out' also reads as burst out laughing or burst out of a room, neither of which this verb means.

'publish' is right, but 'hand out' names the wrong action for the second sense. herausgeben is handing something over or giving it back to its owner — surrendering documents, giving change (Geld herausgeben) — not distributing copies to a group, which is verteilen or austeilen. A learner taking 'hand out' at face value would produce 'Flyer herausgeben', which German does not say. candidate_glosses index 1 has it as 'to hand over, to give, to restitute'; the safe fix is to keep the publishing sense the gloss already leads with and drop the misleading second term.
